title: Reconcile orphaned usage events after API key rotation causing cross-project billing spikes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Short summary: Multiple customers reported sudden billing spikes and quota enforcement anomalies after API key rotations and sub-account merges. Investigation shows a class of 'orphaned usage events' where tokenized request logs lose project/workspace attribution during or immediately after rotation, and are later re-ingested with incorrect tenant pointers. This results in multi-tenant billing misattribution, unexpected quota exhaustion for unrelated projects, and rate-limit violations.

Observed behavior:
- During key rotation windows, a small percentage (~0.3%) of requests are logged with a null or legacy workspace_id and later re-processed by the async usage pipeline with a fallback mapping that picks the oldest matching org, often a parent workspace, causing cross-project charges.
- Rate limiter consults mapping cache that is updated asynchronously; concurrent rotation + requests can consult stale mapping and attribute to wrong project until cache TTL expires.
- Sub-account merges trigger similar behavior where historical tokens are re-associated based on email/key prefixes instead of explicit key id, producing attribution drift.

Root cause hypothesis:
1) Non-atomic rotation: rotation writes new key record but does not atomically swap the authoritative token->workspace pointer used by the real-time attribution service.
2) Re-ingest path for delayed logs uses a different mapping index (legacy_account_map) which resolves tokens by heuristic when pointer absent.
3) Rate-limiter reads mapping cache that can be stale during rotation; fallback path chooses first-match instead of failing-safe.

Proposed mitigations & design decisions:
- Short-term hotfix: change re-ingest job to reject events with missing workspace_id and place them into a quarantine queue for manual/backfill reconciliation rather than heuristic reassignment. Add an alert for quarantine growth.
- Fix the rotation flow to use an atomic pointer swap (DB transaction + config-version bump) so live servers always see a consistent mapping. Add middleware that blocks in-flight requests for the duration of the swap if mapping inconsistent.
- Unify mapping indices: migrate usage pipeline to consult the primary token_map service (same source as rate-limiter) and deprecate legacy heuristics.
- Add a backfill reconciliation job that uses linked audit logs, key id signatures, and PRS to reassign orphaned events deterministically and write correction entries for billing reconciliation.
- Add regression tests and a chaos test that rotates keys under load and checks for no attribution drift.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy hotfix to re-ingest job and quarantine path (canary 10% of ingestion traffic) and run for 48h while monitoring quarantine rate.
2) Ship atomic pointer swap implementation behind feature flag; test in staging with synthetic load, then canary 5% for 24h.
3) Migrate usage pipeline to primary token_map service in a read-only compatibility mode, then switch to authoritative.
4) Run deterministic backfill for events in the quarantine queue with audit confirmation; publish customer-facing reconciliation report and credits where needed.

Metrics & alerts to add:
- Gauge: orphaned_events_quarantine_count (alert P0 at >100/hour)
- Histogram: attribution_latency_ms during rotations
- Counter: reassignments_by_backfill
- Dashboard: billing_misattribution_by_org with absolute cost impact for past 30d

QA & validation:
- Unit tests for pointer swap + DB transaction rollback
- Integration tests: synthetic rotation under concurrent requests using local mapping cache with zero TTL
- End-to-end test: simulate sub-account merge and assert no historical attribution changes

Stakeholders & communication:
- Notify SRE and Billing teams; prepare customer comms template and a DOI (incident) if credits are issued.
- Customer-impact list: affected orgs will be compiled by analytics by 2026-03-14. We will propose credits and detailed timeline.

Notes & links:
- Incident writeup draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/billing/orphaned-usage-rotations
- Initial investigation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4127
- Dashboard link (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/usage-attribution

Open questions:
- Should the rotation middleware block in-flight requests, or implement optimistic mapping with retry semantics?
- What's the acceptable quarantine SLA before we perform deterministic backfill (manual verification required)?
updates: 2026-02-28: Report received from Observability that billing spikes correlated with multiple key rotation windows. Assigned to Omar for investigation. Initial triage points to re-ingest anomalies.

2026-03-03: Reproduced in staging by running rotation script while generating high-concurrency requests. Found 0.3% of events missing workspace_id in the real-time pipeline. Implemented local patch to log full payloads for these events for debugging.
2026-03-05: Confirmed root cause is non-atomic pointer swap and legacy heuristic in the batch re-ingest job. Created design doc for atomic rotation and unified mapping (see Confluence link).
2026-03-07: Hotfix for re-ingest quarantine path landed (PR #4127). Deployed to canary (10% ingestion). Quarantine count initial spike to 120 events/hour, stable after config tweak.
2026-03-10: Atomic pointer swap implementation landed behind flag (PR #4192). Planning staging load tests; targeting canary rollout 2026-03-13.

2026-03-12: Added backfill reconciliation implementation to branch billing-reconcile (PR #4220). Added quota and rate-limiter TTL metric to the runtime. Preparing customer impact list and credit plan.
